newsitem.title: USA: U.S. begins deportation proceeding in Nazi case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. begins deportation proceeding in Nazi case.

text.p: The Justice Department said on Thursday it has begun deportation proceedings against a 74-year-old Michigan man found to have been a Nazi concentration camp guard during the Second World War.
It said the case involved Ferdinand Hammer, a retired foundry supervisor from Sterling Heights who was stripped of his U.S. citizenship by a federal judge in May.

The judge found that Hammer had been an armed guard at the infamous Auschwitz death camp complex in Poland and the Sachsenhausen concentration camp in Germany. He also served as a guard on inmate transfers between Nazi camps.
The judge agreed with the Justice Department that Hammer had concealed from U.S. authorities his Nazi past when he applied for U.S. citizenship in 1963.

The Justice Department said court papers filed on Thursday in U.S. Immigration Court in Detroit argue that Hammer should be deported for his participation in persecution in association with the Nazi government as a armed death camp guard.
"We intend to seek Hammer's expeditious removal from this country," said Eli Rosenbaum, head of the Justice Department's Nazi-hunting Office of Special Investigations.
Department officials said it would be up to Hammer during the deportation proceedings to pick a country he would go to.
